description: The figure is a multi-level pie (sunburst) chart representing medical ethics principles and their associated subtopics, with 4 main inner slices and multiple outer slices; the inner ring contains Beneficence (teal/blue, the largest slice at roughly about half of the circle), Autonomy (green, roughly about a quarter), Non-Maleficence (purple, roughly about a sixth), and Justice (brown, roughly about a tenth). The outer ring subdivides each principle into labeled categories with similarly tinted shades: Beneficence includes “Recognize the Responsibility of the Occupation,” “Comply with Laws and Regulations,” “Provide Medical Care to Patients,” “Continual Learning,” “Provide Assistance in Emergency,” “Respect and Cooperate with Colleagues,” “Respect Life, Dignity of Patients,” “Give top Priority to Patient’s Interest in Conflict of Interest,” “Minimizing Conflicts of Interest,” “Ethical research,” and “Open Discussion and Fair Charging of Fees,” each appearing as relatively small, similarly sized wedges; Autonomy includes “Physician Can Freely Choose Whom to Serve,” “Make Responsible and Independent Clinical Judgement,” “Professional Relationship with Patients and Their Relatives,” “Keep Confidential of Patient’s Information,” “Maintain Truthful, Factual Communication,” “Respect Patient’s Rights to be Informed, Freedom of Choice,” and “Informed Decision-making of Incompetent/Competent Patient,” shown as several medium-to-small green wedges; Non-Maleficence includes “Prevent Patient from Harm,” “Maintain Qualified When Providing Medical Care,” “Report Unethical and Unprofessional Conduct,” and “Do Not Use Medicine for Personal Gain,” shown as a few purple wedges; and Justice includes “Treat Patients Fairly and Equally,” “Allocate Medical Sources Fairly,” “Promote Environmental Sustainability,” and “Promote the Health of Community and Public Education,” shown as a few brown wedges. The chart uses direct text labels on slices (no separate legend and no numeric percentage labels), and no slices appear exploded or otherwise visually emphasized beyond color grouping; the wedges are arranged contiguously around the circle without an explicit descending-size ordering among the outer segments.
